This appeal coming on for hearing this day, Hon'ble Shri Justice Milind Ramesh Phadke passed the following:
 ORDER 1.

This first appeal under Section 28 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (for short "the Act") is preferred against the judgment and decree dated 12.03.2021 passed in RCSHM Case No.267 of 2019 Smt Mahadevi W/O Mukesh Kumar Dhakad vs Mukesh Kumar Dhakad on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46203713/
1 by the Principal Judge, Family Court Shivpuri,
whereby the application preferred by the respondent for Restitution of Conjugal Rights under section 9 of the Act, had been allowed.

2. Short facts of the case are that on 11.07.2008 marriage was solemnized between the appellant/wife and respondent/husband as per Hindu rights and rituals at Village Gopalpur, Tehsil Vijaypur, District Sheopur.
After the marriage two sons, namely, Shivam and Satyam were born out of the wedlock.

In the year, 2012 when respondent/husband had gone to Africa on Government duty being a CRPF constable, he gave his ATM Card to the appellant/wife for procuring the basic household articles and maintain herself and children, but he found that the appellant/wife had given Rs.2,50,000/- to her father.

Thereafter, appellant/wife gave at times Rs.50,000/- and Rs.1,00,000/- whenever the respondent/husband used to be out of service and whenever he used to ask about the same, appellant/wife used to tell him that her father is in need of money since he is facing number of criminal cases.
3. On 29.04.2017 when the respondent/husband was on duty at Pulgaon, the appellant/wife fled away along with some unknown person by taking with her 15 tola gold ornaments and cash and their two sons.

When the parents of the respondent/husband did not find the appellant at home, they informed respondent and in turn the respondent made a complaint to Senior Superintendent of Police, Sheopur, DIG, Gwalior, Station Incharge, P.S. Vijaypur and CEO of his unit.

Prior to the aforesaid incident, the appellant/wife had given approximately Rs.7 lakhs to her father and whenever the respondent/husband had asked her to get the money back, she used to fight with him and even upon ill advice of her parents, she underwent family planning operation without consulting with the respondent/husband.

4. Though appellant had left the house of the respondent/husband on her own volition, she moved an application under Section 125 Cr.P.C for maintenance, wherein the Court has directed the respondent/husband to pay maintenance to the wife and children and when on 11.10.2019 the respondent/husband appeared in the proceedings under Section 128 Cr.P.C in pursuance to the recovery warrant, he was threatened for life by the appellant and her family members that if he does not pay Rs.20,000/- per month towards maintenance to the appellant, he will have to face dire consequences.

Since the appellant had left the respondent/husband and even was not letting the respondent/husband to meet the children and was not fulfilling her marital duties though the respondent/husband wanted to live with her, therefore, an application under Section 9 of the Act came to be filed on behalf of the respondent/husband.
5. A written statement was filed on behalf of the present appellant, wherein the allegations levelled against her were denied in toto.

It was averred in the written statement that when the respondent/husband had left for Africa in the year 2012 on duty, he had not made any arragnement for their livelihood, therefore, under compulsion she had to beg from her father.

It was further submitted that the allegation of leaving the house of the respondent on 29.04.2017 along with gold ornaments and children is baseless and since the respondent was not maintaining her and their children, she had to made a complain at P.S. Vidisha and had to get the recovery warrant issued on 13.03.2019 from the office of SDO.
Further, it was denied that till the date of filing of the written statement, she had passed of Rs. 7 lakhs to her father.

It was also averred therein that the Smt Mahadevi W/O Mukesh Kumar Dhakad vs Mukesh Kumar Dhakad on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46203713/

Thus, it was prayed that the present application be dismissed.

In support of the contentions, the respondent/husband examined himself as AW1, but the appellant/wife did not appear in the witness box and, therefore, vide order dated 05.03.2021 she was proceeded ex parte.

The learned trial Court after appreciating oral and documentary evidence available on record allowed the application for restitution of conjugal rights and directed the respondent/husband to take the appellant/wife back within two months and the appellant/wife was directed to go along with the respondent/husband and perform her marital duties.
8. Aggrieved by the aforesaid, the present appeal has been filed.
Arguments.

9. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the trial Court has not appreciated the evidence of the parties in right perspective, so the findings stand vitiated and the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside.

It is further submitted that the learned trial Court has committed grave error in declaring the appellant ex-parte on 05.03.2021 and passing the order dated 12.03.2021 without giving opportunity to the appellant for putting up her case, even when after upsurge of Covid-19, the Courts had become dormant and were not functioning properly and when the cases were adjourned by the Courts itself due to lockdown or Covid-19, therefore, it was difficult to know the exact dates of proceedings and from perusal of the proceedings, from 09.11.2019 to 25.02.2021 on each and every date the advocate for appellant was present, and it was only on 05.03.2021 that the advocate of appellant was not present and pertinently which was the time of second wave of pandemic and on the same day, appellant was declared ex-parte and the matter was listed for final hearing on 06.03.2021 and on dated 12.03.2021
ex parte decree in the above said matter was passed by the trial Court , which is per se illegal.

10. It was further submitted that the learned trial Court has committed grave error in not considering the conduct of respondent herein, as many complaints have been filed by the appellant against him in respect of cruelty and demand of dowry by the respondent and his family members.

sentences.text:
In the said complaint it was also stated that after leaving for Africa by respondent, his family members had brutally beaten her up and had thrown her along with her bags and baggage out of the house and had also snatched her two sons, for which she had to file an application before the SDM demanding their custody, thereafter, during the pendency of the case her sons were returned back to her, which made respondent furious, resulting his anger bestowed upon the household articles,
which made the appellant to lodge an FIR against respondent under Sections 341, 323, 294, 506 and 427 of IPC about respondent coming and breaking the phone of appellant and trying to take the sons forcibly.
11.
It was further submitted that the learned trial Court has miserably erred in looking the conduct of respondent who has not even complied with the orders of the learned Magistrate.

Instant appellant has filed an application under Section 125 of Cr.P.C wherein after considering the pleadings, documents and arguments of the parties, an order for interim maintenance has been passed in favour of present appellant and directed the respondent to give Rs.3000/- as maintenance to the appellant and Rs.3000/- each for her both sons, therefore, in total Rs.9000/- has been directed to be given to the appellant and her both sons which has not been paid by the respondent,
for the period of last one year, because of which an application under Section 128 of Cr.P.C. for recovery of maintenance amount was filed by the appellant.

It is also submitted that in cross-examination of respondent, he has categorically admitted that a search warrant has been issued against him or his family members from the SDM Court for forcibly taking sons of present appellant, thus, the order of restitution of conjugal rights passed by the trial Court deserves to be set aside.
12.

It was further contended that the learned trial Court had not taken into consideration the on going scenario at the time of proceeding appellant ex parte, as at that time, the second wave was on its peak and the situation was much dire and the present appellant was residing outside the local limits of District Shivpuri, therefore, she was not in a position to come before learned trial Court for recording her evidence, therefore, the impugned order passed by the trial Court is perverse and deserves to be set aside.

It is also submitted that the proceedings of Domestic Violence and cruelty under Section 498A of IPC is also pending consideration before the competent court, therefore, it would endanger her life and liberty if she is compelled to live with the respondent, thus, it was prayed the appeal be allowed and the decree for restitution of conjugal rights passed in favour of respondent/husband be set aside.

13. None for the respondent.
14.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and perused the record.

15. The basic issue which has been raised by the counsel for the appellant is that the learned Trial Court in a very haphazard manner had not given an opportunity of hearing to the appellant/wife to adduce her evidence in support of her contentions raised in the written statement with regard to the harassment committed by the family members of the respondent/husband and regarding the alleged false allegations levelled against her about running away with some unknown person along with the jewellery and two sons.

sentences.text: Proceedings of the learned Family Court were brought to the notice of this Court and upon perusal of the aforesaid proceedings, it is observed that on 10.02.2021 the present respondent/applicant had closed his evidence and the Family Court had listed the matter for the evidence of the present appellant/wife on 18.02.2021.

On 18.02.2021 time was sought for leading evidence on behalf of the appellant which was granted and the next date fixed was 25.02.2021 and on that date again time was sought which was also granted and the matter was directed to be listed on 05.03.2021 and on that date as neither the appellant nor her counsel was present before the Court till 4:30 PM, appellant was, therefore, proceeded ex parte and the matter was directed to be listed on the very next day i.e. 06.03.2021 for the final arguments and on 06.03.2021 upon time sought by the counsel for the respondent the matter was directed to be listed on 12.03.2021 and on the said date the matter was finally heard and was posted for orders and on the very same date judgment was passed and decree was prepared.
17. Admittedly, it is of common knowledge that second wave of pandemic Covid-19 started in the month of March, 2021 and lasted till May, 2021 which was more devastating than the first wave.

Though there is no material available on record to show that the appellant or her counsel since were suffering from the attack of the virus, but this Court can presume the fear which was in the minds of the people with regard to the safety of their lives which in the case of the present appellant appears to be of grave importance as she was accompanying two kids along with her which could have prevented her from marking her appearance before the Court or even being in touch with the counsel, thus, the learned Family Court was required to take a liberal approach and should have given atleast a reasonable opportunity to the appellant to adduce her evidence in support of the contentions raised in the written statement and only, thereafter, should have passed the order.

18. Learned Family Court even in its judgment has found that the certain allegations levelled by the respondent/husbsand against the wife regarding her eloping with some unknown person on 29.04.2017 to be a false allegation, but in absence of any rebuttal had held that since 09.05.2019 the present appellant had left the company of the respondent/husband to be a truth, thus, when the very allegations made by the respondent/husband have been held to be doubtful, the Family Court was required to be more cautious with regard to some allegations in dealing with the other allegations levelled by the respondent/husband and in that regard opportunity was required to be granted to appellant/wife to lead her evidence which had not been done, which to this Court appears to be a good ground for setting aside the judgment and decree and remitting the matter back to the Family Court for giving opportunity to the appellant/wife to lead her evidence in support of her contentions.

19. Thus, without going into the merits of the matter, this Court deems it expedient to allow this first appeal and while setting aside the judgment and decree dated 12.03.2021 passed by the Principal Judge, Family Court, Shivpuri in RCSHM Case No.267 of 2019 remit the matter back for its fresh adjudication after giving an opportunity to the appellant/wife to lead her evidence and decide the same in accordance with law.
20.

With the aforesaid direction, the first appeal is allowed and the judgment and decree dated 12.03.2021 passed by the Principal Judge, Family Court, Shivpuri in RCSHM Case No.267 of 2019 is Smt Mahadevi W/O Mukesh Kumar Dhakad vs Mukesh Kumar Dhakad on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46203713/
5 hereby set aside.
